newsitem.title: USA: Werner Enterprises raising driver pay.
newsitem.headline: Werner Enterprises raising driver pay.

text.p: Werner Enterprises Inc, a full-service transportation company, said Friday it will increase the pay for its drivers and owner-operators by $0.02 a mile, effective January 1.
Robert Synowicki Jr., chief operating officer at the company, said the full impact of the pay increase could cut quarterly earnings by $0.04 to $0.05 a share if there is no customer reimbursement.
However, he said he expects customers to reimburse Werner for the increased costs, although it might take one or two quarters for full reimbursement.

Synowicki said the pay increase is aimed at attracting and retaining qualified drivers. "There is a real shortage of drivers in our industry," he told Reuters, but added that all of Werner's trucks are currently manned with drivers.
Werner Enterprises said it is taking this "proactive step" to maintain a top driver workforce. It added that it is contacting customers to explain the pay increase and to obtain rate increases.

"Attracting and retaining experienced, qualified drivers has always been a key to the success of Werner," Chairman Clarence Werner said in a statement. "The company recognizes that competitive, economic and other factors are making it increasingly more difficult to attract and retain the type of driver that will allow Werner to grow and to continue to provide premium, on-time delivery service to its customers."
Werner Enterprises manages a fleet of 4,550 tractors, of which 3,780 are company owned and operated and 770 tractors are independentlly owned.
